step1_summary: Chief complaint: Acute onset shortness of breath (SOB) while sitting and watching TV

Symptoms: SOB began ~1 hour prior to call, occurring at rest; new non-productive cough since yesterday; palpitations/heart “really going”; chest feels sore with deep inspiration; no frank chest pain reported at rest
Onset/duration/severity: Sudden onset; duration ~1 hour at time of call; severity not quantified but concerning enough to seek care
Aggravating/alleviating factors: Deep inspiration causes chest soreness; no specific alleviating factors noted
Past medical/surgical history: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; otherwise denies medical problems
Medications/allergies: Took codeine regularly post-op but none for ~1 week; allergic to ibuprofen (reaction unspecified)
Family history: Mother had leg clots (DVT)
Social history: Postpartum at home with baby; partner at work; no tobacco/alcohol/travel data provided

Vital signs/exam: Home pulse count of 30 beats over an unspecified interval; clinician interpreted as slightly tachycardic; patient perceives tachycardia; no other vitals (SpO2, BP, temp) available; no formal physical exam

V: Pulmonary embolism (PE): Postpartum (4 weeks) is a high-risk period for VTE; acute SOB at rest, pleuritic-type soreness with deep breath, tachycardia/palpitations, and family history of DVT support PE.
Deep vein thrombosis with possible PE: Recent C-section and postpartum immobility raise DVT risk that could embolize to lungs; no leg symptoms elicited but still plausible.
I: Viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis: New cough since yesterday could precede or accompany mild viral illness that can cause subjective SOB and palpitations from anxiety.
Community-acquired pneumonia (including atypical/COVID-19): Cough and SOB could be infectious, though abrupt onset and lack of fever/sputum argue somewhat against.
N: Pulmonary neoplasm: Unlikely with acute presentation; included for completeness but no supporting features.
D: Iron-deficiency postpartum anemia: Could cause dyspnea and tachycardia after C-section, but sudden onset over 1 hour is atypical.
I2: Medication effect (opioids): Codeine can cause respiratory depression, but she has not taken it for ~1 week, making this unlikely.
Postoperative complications (atelectasis): Typically immediate postoperative period, not 4 weeks later with abrupt onset.
C: Undiagnosed congenital heart disease: Very unlikely given age and lack of prior symptoms; included only for completeness.
A: Asthma or allergic bronchospasm: No wheeze or known asthma; ibuprofen allergy not currently relevant.
T: Spontaneous pneumothorax: Can cause acute pleuritic pain and SOB at rest; no clear unilateral pleuritic pain or risk factors documented.
E: Peripartum (postpartum) cardiomyopathy: Can present within months postpartum with dyspnea and tachycardia; absence of orthopnea/PND/edema and very acute onset are less typical.
Postpartum thyroiditis (thyrotoxic phase): Could cause palpitations and dyspnea, but the abrupt 1-hour onset and concurrent new cough make this less likely.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Acute onset SOB at rest in a woman 4 weeks postpartum after C-section with reported tachycardia and pleuritic-type soreness strongly suggests PE during a known high-risk VTE window, further supported by family history of DVT.
supporting_evidence: Sudden SOB at rest over ~1 hour
Pleuritic chest discomfort with deep inspiration
Postpartum state 4 weeks after C-section (major VTE risk)
Perceived tachycardia; clinician interpreted pulse as slightly fast
opposing_evidence: No objective hypoxia documented (SpO2 not measured)

opposing_evidence: Very abrupt SOB onset at rest over 1 hour is less typical for simple viral URI
Pleuritic-type soreness and postpartum VTE risk point more toward PE

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Occurs within months postpartum and can present with dyspnea and tachycardia; however, extremely acute onset over 1 hour without orthopnea, edema, or cough productive of frothy sputum is less typical.

opposing_evidence: Abrupt onset of SOB at rest
No fever, chills, or purulent sputum reported
